raw_text:
Below is a 12-week general strength program designed for a 42-year-old male desk worker with a history of L4–L5 disc herniation (8 months post, currently asymptomatic). It respects the physio’s guidance: no heavy spinal loading and no loaded spinal flexion. The plan emphasizes neutral spine, hip hinge proficiency, core stability, unilateral work, and gradual load exposure via lower spinal compression alternatives (e.g., front rack goblet, machine work, landmine, sleds, split squats). It includes mobility, conditioning, and recovery. 

Structure overview
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week (A/B/C), plus 1–2 light conditioning/mobility days.
- Phases:
  1) Phase 1 (Weeks 1–4): Restore movement quality, core stability, tissue tolerance.
  2) Phase 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build strength with controlled progressions; introduce heavier unilateral and machine-based patterns; low-to-moderate spinal loading.
  3) Phase 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidate strength, add power elements (low risk), increase intensity within constraints; prep for future goals.
- Session format: 
  - Prep (breathing + mobility + activation)
  - Main lift 1 (lower focus)
  - Main lift 2 (upper focus)
  - Accessories (unilateral, posterior chain, core, anti-flexion/anti-rotation)
  - Finisher/conditioning (short, joint-friendly)
  - Cooldown (mobility/parasympathetic)
- Loading rules:
  - Avoid: barbell back squats, deadlifts from floor, good mornings, sit-ups/crunches, heavy bent-over rows, Jefferson curls.
  - Prefer: goblet/front rack with dumbbells/kettlebells, trap bar from raised handles (if allowed and pain-free), sleds, machines, landmine variations, step-ups, split squats, hip thrusts, cable rows with chest support, pull-ups/lat pulldowns, anti-rotation core.
  - Work in RPE 6–8 most of the time; leave 2–3 reps in reserve (RIR) early; progress gradually.
  - Maintain neutral spine and brace; no loaded spinal flexion.
- Conditioning: low-impact (bike, elliptical, walking incline, sled push, rowing with neutral spine and hip hinge). 
- Progression: add load 2–5% per week when all reps/sets feel solid at target RPE and technique pristine.

General warm-up and movement prep (all sessions)
- 3–5 min easy cardio.
- Breathing/bracing: 2 sets of 5 slow breaths in 90/90 position, emphasize ribcage expansion and gentle abdominal brace.
- Mobility: 
  - Hip flexor stretch 2x30s/side
  - Hamstring neural glide 2x8/side (no end-range flexion)
  - T-spine extension over foam roller 2x6
  - Ankle rocks 2x10/side
- Activation:
  - Dead bug (arms-only or legs-only) 2x6/side
  - Glute bridge 2x10 (progress to mini-band abduction)
  - Banded face pulls 2x12

Core pillar menu (rotate through, all anti-flexion/anti-rotation/anti-lateral flexion)
- Options: Pallof press, half-kneeling cable chop/lift (neutral spine), side plank, bird dog, suitcase carry, farmer carry (moderate, pain-free), dead bug progressions.
- Cue: neutral spine, stacked ribs over pelvis, smooth breathing.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Movement quality, base strength, tolerance)
- Weekly schedule: 3 strength days (A/B/C), 1–2 light cardio/mobility days (20–30 min).

Week 1
Session A
- Goblet box squat (to bench, neutral spine): 3x8 @ RPE 6
- Half-kneeling single-arm cable row: 3x10/side
- DB RDL to mid-shin with slight knee bend, neutral spine: 3x8 @ RPE 6 (use light load, hinge patterning)
- Split squat (bodyweight or light DBs at sides): 3x8/side
- Pallof press: 3x10/side
- Sled push (light): 6x20 m, walk back rest

Session B
- Hip thrust (barbell pad or DB across hips): 4x8 @ RPE 6–7
- Incline DB press (30–45°): 3x10
- Chest-supported DB row: 3x10
- Step-up (knee height just below 90°): 3x8/side
- Side plank: 3x20–30s/side
- Bike easy-moderate 10–12 min

Session C
- Landmine squat (front-loaded, heels elevated if needed): 3x8 @ RPE 6
- Lat pulldown (neutral grip): 3x10
- Cable or band pull-through (hip hinge): 3x12
- DB reverse lunge (short stride, upright): 3x8/side
- Bird dog: 3x6/side (3s holds)
- Row erg 8–10 min steady

Week 2
- Same structure; add 2.5–5% load where technique solid, or 1 rep/set (e.g., 3x9). Keep RPE ≤7. Maintain box for squats to control depth and spine.

Week 3
- Progress to 4 working sets on main lower movements (goblet squat, hip thrust, landmine squat).
- DB RDL range only to where lumbar neutral can be maintained—no rounding. 3–4x8–10 @ RPE 6–7.
- Carries: add suitcase carry 3x20–30 m/side.

Week 4
- Slight deload/skill week: reduce total volume by ~25% (drop one set on mains and accessories), maintain or slightly reduce load, perfect movement, emphasize tempo (3s eccentric) on squats/hinges.

Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Strength development with controlled loading)
- Introduce moderate-load, joint-friendly options: front-loaded and machine patterns; unilateral emphasis; add intensity via tempo and pauses. Still no heavy spinal compression or loaded flexion.

Week 5
Session A
- Landmine front squat (2–3s eccentric): 4x6–8 @ RPE 7
- Chest-supported row or seal row: 4x8
- Rear-foot elevated split squat (DBs at sides): 3x8/side @ RPE 7
- Hip thrust: 3x8–10 @ RPE 7
- Pallof press iso hold: 3x20–30s/side
- Sled push: 6x25 m, moderate

Session B
- Trap bar deadlift from high handles or 2–3" blocks, light-moderate, neutral spine: 4x5 @ RPE 6–7 (only if pain-free and physio agrees; otherwise continue DB RDLs)
- Incline or flat DB press: 4x6–8 @ RPE 7
- Single-leg RDL (DB, contralateral load, shallow range): 3x8/side
- Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up (neutral grip): 3x8–10
- Side plank with top-leg abduction or suitcase carry: 3x20–30s or 3x25 m/side
- Bike intervals: 6x45s on/60s easy

Session C
- Leg press (feet mid-stance, neutral pelvis): 4x8 @ RPE 7
- Cable or machine chest press: 3x8–10
- Cable pull-through or banded hip hinge: 3x12
- Step-up (slightly higher box than Phase 1): 3x8/side
- Half-kneeling cable lift or anti-rotation press: 3x10/side
- Row erg: 10–12 min, easy-moderate

Week 6
- Progress loads 2–5% if RPE ≤7 and form pristine.
- Add pauses: 1s pause at bottom of landmine squat and at knee level on trap bar (if used).
- Accessories remain 3–4x8–12.

Week 7
- Volume bump: add a set to main lower movement of two sessions (e.g., landmine squat 5 sets, leg press 5 sets) or add a rep within range.
- Hip thrust progress to 4x6–8 slightly heavier.
- Introduce supported single-arm DB row (knee on bench) 3x10/side to vary angles.

Week 8
- Deload: reduce sets by ~30–40%, maintain technique, RPE ~6. Keep pattern familiarity. If any back tightness appears, regress ROM or load and emphasize bracing.

Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Consolidation, power emphasis, readiness)
- Maintain constraints; add low-risk power (med ball, sled), slightly higher intensities on safe patterns.

Week 9
Session A
- Landmine squat: 5x5 @ RPE 7–8 (no grinders)
- Med ball chest pass or scoop toss (against wall, 2–4 kg): 4x5–6 reps (explosive, perfect posture)
- RFESS (DBs): 4x6–8/side
- Hip thrust: 4x6–8
- Pallof press to overhead (anti-extension): 3x8/side
- Sled push heavy-moderate: 6x20 m

Session B
- Trap bar deadlift high handles OR DB RDL if not using trap bar: 5x3–5 @ RPE 7–8 (no valsalva to excess; crisp reps)
- DB bench press (heavier): 4x5–6
- Chest-supported row (heavier): 4x6–8
- Single-leg hip hinge cable reach (light): 3x10/side
- Suitcase carry: 4x25–30 m/side

Session C
- Leg press (heavier): 5x5–6 @ RPE 7–8
- Neutral-grip pull-up (assisted as needed) or lat pulldown: 4x6–8
- Landmine single-arm press (half-kneeling): 3x6–8/side
- Step-down (control eccentric): 3x8/side
- Side plank: 3x30–40s/side
- Row/bike 8–10 min easy

Week 10
- Small load increases if bar speed and technique solid.
- Add cluster option on med ball: 2 reps, 10s rest, 2 reps x 3 clusters per set.
- Maintain RPE caps ≤8.

Week 11
- Keep intensity; slightly reduce accessories to keep freshness.
- Hip thrust 3x5–6 @ RPE 7–8.
- Landmine squat 4x4–5 with 2–3s eccentric to reinforce control.

Week 12 (Peak technique and reassess)
- Option A (taper feel): reduce volume 30–40%, keep intensity moderate; focus on fast concentric, pristine form.
- Option B (if client eager): maintain Week 11 loads, fewer sets, assess rep-quality PRs on:
  - Landmine squat AMRAP at RPE 8 cap (leave 2 RIR)
  - Hip thrust rep-quality set
  - RFESS rep-quality set/side
  - Chin/pulldown reps at fixed load
- Finish with med ball power and easy conditioning.

Accessory and technique notes
- Bracing: teach “exhale to stack” then gentle brace before each rep. Avoid breath-holding to redline; use submax valsalva only if client is well-coached and symptom-free.
- ROM: Stop any lower-body hinge/squat ROM where lumbar neutrality is compromised. Depth is earned, not forced.
- Tempo: Use controlled eccentrics (2–3s) on squats/hinges to increase stimulus without heavy loads.
- Grip positions: Favor neutral grips for pressing/pulling to reduce shoulder stress.
- Machines: Chest-supported row, leg press, hamstring curl, cable stacks are your friends to load tissues while safeguarding the spine.

Conditioning and lifestyle (2x/week on non-lifting days)
- 20–30 min low-impact cardio (bike, brisk walk incline, elliptical) at conversational pace.
- Optional 6–8 strides of 10–15s on/45s off on bike if tolerated.
- Daily walks 20–30 min to reduce sedentary time.

Recovery and mobility
- Daily micro-breaks: stand/walk 5 min every 45–60 min of desk work.
- Post-session cooldown: 5 min easy cardio + mobility circuit (hip flexor stretch, piriformis stretch, T-spine rotation, calf stretch).
- Sleep: 7–9 hours; consistent schedule.
- Monitor: any back discomfort >3/10, lingering >24–48h, or radiating symptoms—regress load/ROM, skip provocative moves, and communicate with physio.

Progression guidelines
- When all sets land ≤ target RPE with excellent technique for two consecutive sessions, add 2–5% load next time or add a rep within range.
- If any set exceeds RPE 8 or form degrades, hold or reduce load, or trim a set.
- Prioritize unilateral lower body strength (RFESS, step-ups) as primary progressive overload drivers.

Optional weekly layout example
- Mon: Session A
- Wed: Session B
- Fri: Session C
- Tue/Sat: 20–30 min cardio + mobility (optional)

Exercise substitutions (if equipment or tolerance varies)
- Landmine squat → Goblet front squat to box
- Trap bar high handle → DB RDL or cable pull-throughs
- Hip thrust → Smith hip thrust or glute bridge
- Chest-supported row → Seated cable row with chest support pad
- Leg press → Hack squat (light, neutral, limited depth) or sled drags

Nutrition (general, assuming no specific requests/constraints)
- Protein: ~1.6–2.0 g/kg/day spread over 3–4 meals.
- Carbs: Emphasize around training windows for energy.
- Fats: 0.6–1.0 g/kg/day.
- Hydration: 30–35 mL/kg/day; add 500–750 mL around training.
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day if no contraindications.

Key coaching cues
- “Ribs down, belt buckle up” to stack torso.
- “Hips back, knees soft” for hinge; “sit between your heels” for squat.
- “Own the pause” at bottom positions; move smoothly, avoid bounce.
- “Stop where your spine stays neutral.”

This plan builds general strength while carefully managing spinal load and eliminating loaded spinal flexion. Reassess weekly tolerance, and maintain communication with the physio for any progression beyond these constraints.
